A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCA research work. Their complete main texts, figures, equations, references, and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison. Duplicated panels in v3 are document-level issues, not extraction gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original stability and accuracy experiments on ImageNet and TweetEval, plus a synthetic comparison of random masking and random flipping.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical studies and adds attribution-size sensitivity results and measured batching performance.

M1.justification: The SCA estimator, uniform additive-mask sampling, Gumbel-based sampling implementation, and optional multiplicative smoothing remain unchanged. The new batching study does not introduce a different certification algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ImageNet subset, six TweetEval tasks, and synthetic Fourier-spectrum experiment. The added attribution-size and timing studies operate within this existing coverage. Appendix C corrects 'two classes per sample' to 'two images per class,' matching v1's main-text description.

E2.justification: MuS remains the certification comparator, and both versions evaluate LIME, SHAP, Integrated Gradients, MFABA, and random attributions. The new timing table introduces batching controls and a single-forward-pass reference, without adding an alternative certification or attribution method.

E3.justification: New experiments evaluate top-12.5%, 37.5%, and 50% attribution selections alongside the existing 25%, and measure batching with sizes 5, 10, and 15 over 100 dataset samples per model. Existing SCA settings, including N=150 and epsilon=delta=0.1, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.4 adds sensitivity analysis of attribution size, addressing dependence on the original fixed 25% selection. Appendix C.6 adds computational-efficiency analysis across batch sizes. Existing smoothing and random-masking-versus-flipping analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 1,000 bootstrap iterations for 95% confidence intervals. v3's timing table adds values with ± terms but does not specify a distinct uncertainty-estimation procedure or changed seed/repeated-run practice; additional timing statistics alone do not establish such a change.

E6.justification: v3 adds attribution-size curves and timing results; Table 1 reports ResNet50 at 3.82 ms per baseline pass versus 0.40 ms effective time with batch size 15. Figure 6 replaces v1's ResNet18 panel with duplicated ResNet50 results. Other principal result figures, including Figure 8's accuracy values, are retained.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 adds an explicit special-case margin definition, gamma=(p1−p2)/2 for sorted class probabilities, with a prediction-preservation explanation. The certification bounds, smoothing results, and proofs in Appendices A and B otherwise retain their mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: soft stability, model-agnostic sampling certification, stronger guarantees than MuS, and a Boolean-analysis characterization of mild smoothing. Revised wording and additional supporting experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly interprets hard stability as robustness to worst-case additive attacks and soft stability through random additive attacks. Appendix C.2 newly acknowledges competitive MuS certificates for small radii on heavily smoothed RoBERTa. The earlier discussion of masking-related missingness bias is removed; the principal Appendix D limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-code availability link on the first page and documents batch sizes, timing measurements, and the 100-sample timing evaluation. The exlib attribution implementation, GPU types, certification parameters, and smoothing sample budgets were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: Sections 2.2 and 6 add closer positioning against Anchors, probabilistic sufficient explanations, formal minimal explanations, and probabilistic Lipschitz analysis of explainer robustness. They emphasize the one-sided nature of additive stability. The central relationship to MuS remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 streamlines the abstract and exposition, condenses related work, combines Discussion and Conclusion into Section 7, and moves general probabilistic-guarantee discussion into Appendix D. The main narrative and technical section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 1 and the multi-panel Figure 11, simplifies Figure 2, adjusts Figure 6's axes, and relocates existing figures. v1 Figures 11–12 become v3 Figures 12–13. Figures 6 and 11 contain duplicated ResNet50 panels, reducing the accuracy of their presentation.

improvement.justification: The attribution-size study tests dependence on the fixed 25% choice, while timing measurements clarify practical certification costs. Added code-access information and closer prior-work comparisons also improve the paper. These limited gains are partly offset by duplicated ResNet50 panels in Figures 6 and 11, which displace the original Figure 6 ResNet18 comparison, and an unchanged limitation claiming that only 25% selection was studied.
